newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end little changed, eye on CPI data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end little changed, eye on CPI data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in quiet trade on Monday, tracking U.S. treasuries for much of the session, with both markets focused on the release on Tuesday of key U.S. inflation data, analysts said.

"It was very, very light activity all day and we basically just tracked the U.S.," said a bond trader with one bank-owned brokerage. "Most people are waiting around until tomorrow, but there was just a general lack of interest."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.07 to C$107.02 to yield 7.388 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 7.17 percent. The spread between the two narrowed to 22 basis points from 24 basis points at Friday's close.

Analysts said the focus for the market was U.S. consumer price index data for March due out on Tuesday. The data were seen as key indicators of the next move in U.S. interest rates and had implications for both Canadian bonds and the currency.
Canada's dollar weakened to another two-year low on Monday. The currency has weakened in recent weeks on concerns the Bank of Canada will not match another U.S. rate hike.
Today's weakness prompted the Bank of Canada to buy Canadian dollars to defend the currency.

Canadian markets continued "to mark time today in advance of the looming U.S. CPI numbers due out Tuesday. The pressure on the Canadian dollar continues to mount and the concern of the Bank of Canada is evidenced in their frequency of intervention," said Technical Data analyst David Ebata in a commentary.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.10 to C$100.80 to yield 6.883 percent, while the U.S. bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.98 percent.
